roadmap_item: §5 after item 7c (M1c): a multi-target compiled choice on the held-out pairs
question: M1c found that the compiled programme's target choice, one target gene per element, keeps 39 of the 1,918 held-out ENCODE CRISPRi pairs in K562 and weakens the anchor's gain over activity and distance from +0.1361 [95% CI 0.0749, 0.2258] to +0.0792 [0.0282, 0.1562]; 1,209 of the pairs sit on compiled elements whose single rule names another gene. Does a compiled target choice that keeps every protein-coding gene the compiler's own bar names at an element (enhancer_target.MIN_EFFECT, 0.1 log2, by the size rule predict_target names the compiled target with), nothing tuned, rank the same held-out pairs better than the one-target choice, by the anchor's metric?
population: the 1,918 held-out K562 pairs M1c registered (data/results/signaltrace_registration.json, population_ids and population_sha256), as crispri.load reads them from the held-out file pinned by sha256, in file order; the label is the file's Regulated column. Every choice is read on all of them: a pair a choice does not keep stays in the population with 0 in that choice's two columns. The fit rows are M1c's and the anchor's: the K562 training pairs (EPCrisprBenchmark training_K562, the split the project's CRISPRi benchmark fits on) that crispri.annotate marks covered
training_split: EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.training_K562.GRCh38 (crispri.TRAINING): every K562 pair of the training file, of which the covered pairs are the fit rows. The census, the choice of TOP_K and every fit read only these; no held-out pair enters a fit or a choice
candidates: the candidate targets of a compiled element, in order: the target its predicted rule names (the compiled programme with its experimental rule lines removed, signaltrace.PREDICTED_ONLY), then every gene of the response cache's window at that element (targets.ElementResponses, threshold 0.0 sweep) that is a protein-coding gene of the chromosome in GENCODE v50 (genome.Annotation.protein_coding, the kind of set the sweep named its compiled target from) and whose predicted size on deletion reaches the compiler's bar, MIN_EFFECT = 0.1 log2 fold change; the size is targets.genes_at_bar's, the larger of the predicted fall and the predicted rise over every track, ties to the fall, strongest first, which is the rule predict_target names the compiled target with. A gene already listed is not listed twice. An element the cache does not hold keeps its compiled target alone

one_target.name: the one-target choice (M1c's s2_target)
one_target.phrase: keeping the one compiled target per element
one_target.kept: an element of the compiled programme that overlaps the CRISPRi element (half-open intervals, signaltrace.ChromLookup.overlapping) carries a predicted rule whose target gene's symbol is the measured gene: signaltrace.trace_pair's s2_target, reproduced pair for pair
one_target.value: the anchor's deletion_drop on kept pairs, 0 otherwise

multi_target.name: the multi-target choice at the compiler's bar (primary)
multi_target.phrase: keeping every coding gene at the compiler's bar
multi_target.kept: an element of the compiled programme that overlaps the CRISPRi element (the same elements and the same overlap search as the one-target choice) lists the measured gene among its candidate targets (CANDIDATES)
multi_target.value: the anchor's deletion_drop on kept pairs, 0 otherwise

top_k.name: the top-k choice, k from the training split (secondary)
top_k.phrase: keeping the first k candidate targets per element
top_k.kept: an element of the compiled programme that overlaps the CRISPRi element lists the measured gene among its first TOP_K candidate targets (CANDIDATES, compiled target first)
top_k.value: the anchor's deletion_drop on kept pairs, 0 otherwise

census_rule: on the fit rows only (the covered K562 training pairs): for each k of K_TRIED, the top-k choice's model (METRIC) is fitted on the fit rows and its average precision is read on the same fit rows; TOP_K is the smallest k with the largest average precision. If TOP_K is 1 the top-k choice is the one-target choice and is not read; if no compiled element reached by a fit row lists more than TOP_K candidates it is the multi-target choice and is not read. Written before the census was computed

anchor.model: activity + distance + deletion against activity + distance, weights fitted on the covered K562 training pairs (crispri.score_published), average precision, crispri.gain_interval

metric: the anchor's metric, unchanged (signaltrace.METRIC). A choice's model is activity + distance (log_distance, log_activity, activity_over_distance) plus the choice's two columns, kept (0 or 1) and value, both 0 for a pair the choice does not keep. Each model is fitted by crispri.logistic_fit (lam 1e-3, 25 rounds) on the fit rows and scored on the 1,918 population pairs; the score is average precision (crispri.average_precision). The primary reading is the multi-target choice's average precision minus the one-target choice's, with the 95% interval of crispri.gain_interval; beside it, by the same paired resampling, each choice's gain over activity + distance and its difference from the anchor

bootstrap.unit: chromosome: whole chromosomes resampled with replacement, the anchor's unit

decision: for the multi-target choice (primary) and, when it is read, the top-k choice (secondary), with [dlo, dhi] the 95% interval of its average precision minus the one-target choice's and [alo, ahi] that of its average precision minus the anchor's: NONE_ADDED if it keeps no population pair the one-target choice does not keep; else BETTER if dlo > 0, worded by the anchor: BETTER_BELOW_ANCHOR if ahi < 0, BETTER_ABOVE_ANCHOR if alo > 0, otherwise BETTER_NO_DIFFERENCE_FROM_ANCHOR; WORSE if dhi < 0; otherwise NO_BETTER. The falsifier is the primary's NO_BETTER, WORSE or NONE_ADDED: then the multi-target choice is no better than the one-target choice on these pairs. The question is answered by the primary alone; the secondary is read beside it and decides nothing. No margin beyond the intervals is applied
stop_rule: one run, from this registration's committed code, on the cached files the registration pins by sha256. No choice, column, population, fit row, metric, parameter or rule is changed after the multi-target choice is read on any held-out pair; a defect found afterwards is reported beside the registered readings and corrected only under a new registration. The run stops with HARNESS_DEFECT, before the multi-target or top-k choice is read on the population, if: a pinned input moved; the population's ids or sha256 differ from M1c's registration; the removed experimental lines of a program differ from readergate.rule_targets' count; a pair kept by the one-target choice is not kept by the top-k choice, or one kept by the top-k choice is not kept by the multi-target choice; the one-target columns differ from M1c's committed s2_target columns for any population pair; the anchor does not reproduce the committed arm-1 figures exactly (1,918 pairs, 118 positives, gain 0.1361, interval [0.0749, 0.2258]); or the one-target choice does not reproduce M1c's committed s2_target reading exactly (39 kept, 35 regulated, gain 0.0792 [0.0282, 0.1562], against the anchor -0.0569 [-0.097, -0.0248])

outcomes.HARNESS_DEFECT: stopped before the multi-target choice was read on the held-out pairs: {what}
outcomes.NONE_ADDED: no pair added: {phrase} keeps no held-out K562 pair beyond the one-target choice's ({k} of the {n} pairs kept, {kp} of them regulated), so on these pairs target choice cannot rank the measured pairs differently; against the one-target choice {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}] in average precision
outcomes.BETTER_BELOW_ANCHOR: better than the one-target choice and below the anchor: {phrase} ranks the {n} held-out K562 pairs better than keeping one target per element, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}] in average precision ({k} pairs kept, {kp} of them regulated, against {k1} and {kp1}); its gain over activity and distance is {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}], the one-target choice's {g1} [95% CI {lo1}, {hi1}]; it stays below the anchor, {a} [95% CI {alo}, {ahi}]
outcomes.BETTER_NO_DIFFERENCE_FROM_ANCHOR: better than the one-target choice: {phrase} ranks the {n} held-out K562 pairs better than keeping one target per element, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}] in average precision ({k} pairs kept, {kp} of them regulated, against {k1} and {kp1}); its gain over activity and distance is {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}], the one-target choice's {g1} [95% CI {lo1}, {hi1}]; against the anchor {a} [95% CI {alo}, {ahi}], no difference detected
outcomes.BETTER_ABOVE_ANCHOR: better than the one-target choice and above the anchor: {phrase} ranks the {n} held-out K562 pairs better than keeping one target per element, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}] in average precision ({k} pairs kept, {kp} of them regulated, against {k1} and {kp1}), and better than the anchor, {a} [95% CI {alo}, {ahi}]; its gain over activity and distance is {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}], the one-target choice's {g1} [95% CI {lo1}, {hi1}]
outcomes.NO_BETTER: no better than the one-target choice: between {phrase} and keeping one target per element no difference was detected on the {n} held-out K562 pairs, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}] in average precision ({k} pairs kept, {kp} of them regulated, against {k1} and {kp1}); its gain over activity and distance is {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}], the one-target choice's {g1} [95% CI {lo1}, {hi1}]; against the anchor {a} [95% CI {alo}, {ahi}]
outcomes.WORSE: worse than the one-target choice: {phrase} ranks the {n} held-out K562 pairs below keeping one target per element, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}] in average precision ({k} pairs kept, {kp} of them regulated, against {k1} and {kp1}); its gain over activity and distance is {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}], the one-target choice's {g1} [95% CI {lo1}, {hi1}]; against the anchor {a} [95% CI {alo}, {ahi}]

limitations: both choices carry the anchor's deletion_drop as their value, so the comparison isolates which pairs each keeps; it says nothing about the value a compiled rule states or about the stages after it, where M1c lost every pair at the bridge

the protein-coding set is GENCODE v50 as the project's annotation reads it now; the sweep named its compiled targets from a coding set of its own day, so a compiled target that is not the first coding gene at the bar is possible and is counted beside the readings; the compiled target is kept whatever the set says
the candidate targets and the anchor's two columns come from one AlphaGenome sweep, and AlphaGenome was trained on ENCODE; the multi-target choice is not independent of the anchor's value column

the held-out file's positives were filtered on chromatin at the tested element (crispri.POSITIVE_FILTER) and the activity column reads H3K27ac from the same file; both choices share that baseline, so it cancels from the choice-to-choice difference and not from a gain over activity and distance
the metric ranks all 1,918 pairs; a choice that keeps few of them can move the ranking of those few only. The kept counts stand beside every reading for that reason
no choice is a test of a mechanism: a better ranking says only that the compiled layer, at target choice, ranks the measured pairs better when it keeps more targets
descriptives_not_verdicts: per choice: the pairs kept of the 1,918 and of the fit rows, how many of them regulated, how many with a value above 0, and its fitted weights
the population pairs the multi-target choice keeps and the one-target choice does not, and how many of them regulated; where the measured gene sits among an element's candidate targets
the candidate-target census of the compiled elements on the chromosomes read: how many hold 2 or more, how many are not cached, how many compiled targets are not the first coding gene at the bar
falsifier: the primary's NO_BETTER, WORSE or NONE_ADDED: the multi-target choice is then no better than the one-target choice on these pairs
exploration_preceded_this: stated so that nothing here is read as blind to figures this lane had seen. Before writing it the lane read: M1c's committed figures (signaltrace_result.json: the anchor's 1,918 pairs, 118 positives, top_target kept 40 with 36 regulated; s2_target kept 39 with 35 regulated, gain +0.0792 [0.0282, 0.1562], against the anchor -0.0569 [-0.0970, -0.0248], dropped because 'the overlapping elements name another gene' 1,209 and 'no compiled element overlaps' 670; 9,237 fit rows, 245 kept by s2_target with 188 regulated) and M1c's code; the shape of the response cache (one chr21 record); a parse of chr21's compiled program (5,174 predicted rules, one per element); the training census (data/results/targetchoice_census.json, 3d85122), and before it a dry run of the same census on the chr21 and chr22 training pairs only; and, after TOP_K was fixed from the census, a dry run of the run's code path with a TRAINING stand-in for the population (every fifth training pair scored, the other four fifths as fit rows, the anchor and comparator checks bypassed, the held-out file not parsed, written to a scratch directory), whose reading on that training stand-in was NO_BETTER, +0.0576 [95% CI -0.0177, +0.1163] for the multi-target choice against the one-target choice (72 pairs kept against 43). No parameter or rule was changed after it. This lane computed no choice on any held-out pair before this file was committed (the one-target choice's held-out figures above are M1c's committed ones); the choices were exercised only on the training split and on the synthetic programs of tests/test_targetchoice.py
departures: the primary multi-target choice takes the compiler's own bar (enhancer_target.MIN_EFFECT) and no parameter, as the brief preferred; the top-k choice is secondary, its k fixed on the training split by CENSUS_RULE (in-sample average precision on the fit rows), and decides nothing
the training split is the one the project's CRISPRi benchmark fits on, EPCrisprBenchmark training_K562: 9,237 covered K562 pairs, 451 regulated, the anchor's and M1c's fit rows

the value column of every choice is the anchor's deletion_drop, as in M1c's s2_target, so the comparison changes only which pairs are kept; the value a compiled rule would state for a further target is not read
candidate targets are protein-coding genes, the kind of target the compiled programme names (compile.compile_chromosome reads predicted_coding)

frozen_code.tests: tests/test_targetchoice.py (synthetic programs; not on the run's path, not pinned)

money: none: no request is sent and no key is read
network: none: every input is already on this machine

sources.accession: EngreitzLab/CRISPR_comparison EPCrisprBenchmark training_K562 and heldout_5_cell_types (Gschwind et al.)
ENCODE SCREEN cCREs scored by AlphaGenome deletion (all-element table and per-element response cache)
sources.version: the 2026-09 all-element sweep; pinned here by sha256

sources.accession: GENCODE v50 basic annotation, per chromosome

inputs.role: fit rows: the covered K562 training pairs
the population: its K562 pairs, scored
ElementCache and ElementResponses: every gene's deletion response at an element

inputs.path: GENCODE v50 per-chromosome GFF3 (protein-coding symbols, targetchoice.CANDIDATES)

inputs.role: M1c's registration: the population's ids and sha256
M1c's result: the s2_target columns and reading the one-target choice must reproduce
the training census that fixed TOP_K

parameters.fit: crispri.logistic_fit, lam 1e-3, 25 rounds, on the covered K562 training pairs

bootstrap.unit: chromosome: whole chromosomes resampled with replacement, the anchor's unit

exclusions: every stage after the anchor reads the compiled programs with their experimental rule lines removed. Those rules carry the CRISPRi screens' own EffectSize, the held-out file's pairs included (marked 'held-out split, evaluation only, never a feature'), and the bridge prefers an experimental rule to a predicted one for the same mechanism (bridge.PRECEDENCE), so a stage that read them would read the outcome. The removed lines are counted per program and must equal readergate.rule_targets' count of experimental rule lines; nothing else in a program is changed
held-out pairs in cell types other than K562: the anchor is a K562 result
a pair a choice does not keep is kept in the population with 0 in that choice's two columns

partitions.training: the fit rows only: the covered K562 training pairs; TOP_K was fixed on them
partitions.heldout: the scored population: the held-out file's K562 pairs; no held-out pair enters a fit

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 79aa1e2

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
